newsitem.title: SWEDEN: VOLVO MAY STEP UP CAPACITY AT NEDCAR.
newsitem.headline: VOLVO MAY STEP UP CAPACITY AT NEDCAR.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo may need to borrow capacity from its partner Mitsubishi at the two companies' joint plant in Born, the Netherlands, to meet rising demand, Swedish daily Svenska Dagbladet said on Thursday.

Volvo's production capacity at the plant is 110,000 vehicles per year but right now it is producing cars at an annual rate of 115,000 vehicles and it may need to use capacity from its partner, Japan's Mitsubishi Motors Corp, to meet increasing demand if it continues, the newspaper said.
Volvo and Mitsubishi operate a joint car plant in the Netherlands, which is owned equally by the two companies and the Dutch government.

"If the current trend keeps up -- and all signs say it will -- we may have to borrow a bit of capacity from our cooperation partner, Mitsubishi, to meet production volumes for the year," the newspaper quoted a Volvo spokesman as saying.
The newspaper said the two companies are braced to increase production capacity to 280,000 vehicles from 220,000, divided equally between them.
"It is too early to say when we will reach that, that is 140,000 cars, but it could take place next year if the current strong trend continues," the newspaper quoted the spokesman as saying.
The Nedcar plant at Born produces Volvo's S40/V40 models and Mitsubishi's Charisma.
No one at Volvo was immediately available for comment.
